title: Affine invariance of Lebesgue constants for interpolation nodes

problemStatement.formal: For a<b, the affine map T:[-1,1]->[a,b] preserves Lagrange bases and Lebesgue constants: Lambda(T(nodes),[a,b]) = Lambda(nodes,[-1,1]).
problemStatement.plain: The file proves that interpolation-node questions on arbitrary intervals reduce to the standard interval by an affine change of variables. Chebyshev nodes on [a,b] are the affine images of the usual Chebyshev nodes.
whyMatters: Converts arbitrary-interval interpolation questions into the normalized [-1,1] case.
Shows a previously axiomatized affine-invariance bridge can be proved directly from the Lagrange basis formula.

proven: `affineMap_strictMono` and `affineMap_mem_Icc` prove the affine map preserves order and interval membership.
`lagrangeBasis_affine_covariant` proves Lagrange bases are invariant when both nodes and arguments are transformed.
`lebesgueFunction_affine_invariant` and `lebesgueConstantOnInterval_affine_invariant` prove the Lebesgue function and constant are affine-invariant.
`chebyshev_lebesgue_any_interval`, `chebyshev_one_midpoint`, and `chebyshev_two_formula` specialize the result to Chebyshev nodes.
open: Weighted intervals and orthogonal-polynomial variants remain outside this axiom-free file.
The parent Erdos1129Problem file still contains axiomatized approximation-theory results.
knownResults.goal: Use this axiom-free interval-transfer proof as the reusable bridge before attacking weighted Lebesgue-constant variants.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Eliminated both axioms (2→0). Proved Lagrange basis covariance and Lebesgue constant affine invariance from scratch. File now fully verified (0 axioms, 0 sorries, 15 theorems).

Proved affine map properties: monotonicity, inverse, interval preservation
Chebyshev nodes defined on arbitrary intervals
insights: Lebesgue constant is affine-invariant — reduces all interval problems to [-1,1]
Chebyshev nodes on [a,b] = affine images of standard Chebyshev nodes
For n=1, optimal node on [a,b] is midpoint (a+b)/2
Weight function generalization requires separate techniques (orthogonal polynomials)
c^(n-1) cancellation in Lagrange basis: T(x)-T(y)=c(x-y) means affine map factors out of both numerator and denominator
No DistinctNodes hypothesis needed for covariance — holds for all node configurations
